where: sentence after the formula: 'sont constantes sur S, sauf peut-être pour i = j'
scan: sauf peut-être pour i = j, donc sont toutes constantes
note: Wrong index. Over a field, (iii)_a gives dim H^i(Ω^j) = 0 for i ≠ j, i+j ≠ n, and (iii)_b, (iii)_c give dimension 1 for i = j with 2i ≠ n; the only dimensions (iii) leaves open are those with i + j = n (for fixed j the single index i = n - j), which the alternating-sum argument then settles. With 'i = j' the deduction 'd'après (iii)' does not hold, since i = n - j ≠ j is not covered. Possibly the author's slip rather than a typing error. The TeX keeps the printed reading.

where: displayed formula at the foot of the page, target of the canonical arrow
note: Iterating SGA 4 XIV 3.3 on the d affine pieces of P(E) - Y gives H^q(P(E) - Y) = 0 for q ≥ r+d, so by the local-cohomology sequence the canonical (forget-supports) map H^q_Y(P(E)) -> H^q(P(E)) is bijective for q > r+d and surjective for q = r+d, exactly as stated. With target H^q(Y) the statement fails (q = 2r: H^{2r}_Y(P(E)) ≅ H^{2n}(Y)(-d) ≠ 0, H^{2r}(Y) = 0). The next sentence (p. 49) passes by Poincaré duality to the restriction H^q(P(E)) -> H^q(Y). The TeX keeps the printed reading. (The mark after E on the left side is a ')' whose middle is lost to faint type; not a difference.)
